title: Robin Padilla faces DOJ investigation for obstruction of justice complaint
summary: Senator Robin Padilla on Friday went to the Department of Justice to attend the preliminary investigation on the obstruction of justice complaint filed against him in connection with the alleged…

blocks.text: Senator Robin Padilla on Friday went to the Department of Justice to attend the preliminary investigation on the obstruction of justice complaint filed against him in connection with the alleged escape of Senator Bato dela Rosa from the Senate building.
In a video by Sandra Aguinaldo of GMA News, Julius Henry Balteza, Padilla’s legal counsel, said they are filing a rejoinder in response to the complainant’s reply to their counter-affidavit.
Balteza maintained that Padilla was innocent of the allegations against him.
“For our defense, we maintain na lang ‘yung earlier answers namin na we will not be divulging our answers. Pero to answer that, yes, we maintain po ‘yung innocence ni Senator Padilla,” he said.
(For our defense, we will maintain our previous answer that we will not divulge our answers. But to answer that, yes, we maintain Senator Padilla's innocence.)

On May 28, the Philippine National Police-Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (PNP-CIDG) filed a complaint for obstruction of justice against Padilla and others with the DOJ over the escape of Senator Ronald "Bato" Dela Rosa from the Senate building.

Dela Rosa is the subject of an arrest warrant from the International Criminal Court for “alleged criminal responsibility as an indirect co-perpetrator” in the crimes against humanity of murder during the Duterte administration's war on drugs. He was then chief of the Philippine National Police.
He sought refuge at the Senate on May 11 after authorities attempted to serve the said arrest warrant. However, he slipped out of the Senate building on May 14.
Padilla previously maintained that he did not help Dela Rosa “escape,” as the former police chief only asked to hitch a ride with him out of the Senate building on May 14. —Jamil Santos/LDF, GMA News
